content: Currently, if a PR fills in some proof_wanted/def_wanted from the Wanted folder and deletes the now-empty Wanted file, then it gets the file-removed label. Example: #42414. Could the label ignore files in the Wanted folder? There is little point importing these in downstream repos, so removing such a file shouldn't require a deprecation period.

Tangentially, I'll note this raises a downside of having moved all the wanted statements; the git diff now forces us to re-review that the statement is correct, since it was moved rather than populated in place.
@Damiano Testa How hard would it be to get the lean-aware declaration diff to understand proof_wanted / def_wanted?

I have not looked at the details of the implementation of proof_/def_wanted, but I think that they register private declarations. Right now, the declaration diff in Lean is fully blind to private declarations.
Maybe, if there is a desire for this, we could make the def_/proof_wanted machinery maintain an environment extension and then the declaration diff could read that.

Maybe we should just make proof_- and def_wanted create public declarations? :eyes: We could still make them not show up in autocomplete by making them aux definitions (or such that they otherwise have _ in a leading position of a component, e.g. <namespace>._wanted.proof).

A standard naming scheme could also provide a way to grab all of them—then we could avoid the overhead of an env extension :)
